nb094bab071e.s:
Consider the following statements about the IPC food-insecurity scale:
1. It has five phases.
2. Phase 2 (Stressed) is more severe than Phase 3 (Crisis).
3. Phase 5 is Catastrophe/Famine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nb094bab071e.x: The IPC scale runs Phase 1 Minimal, 2 Stressed, 3 Crisis, 4 Emergency, 5 Catastrophe/Famine; Stressed is less severe than Crisis, so statement 2 is wrong.

na323783aee7.s:
Consider the following statements about education in the Madras Presidency:
1. The Central Collegiate Institute (1841) came before the Noble School at Machilipatnam.
2. Madras University came before the result-based grants-in-aid system.
3. The Noble School was founded after Madras University.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
na323783aee7.x: The order is Central Collegiate Institute (1841), Noble School (1843), Madras University (1857) and result-based grants-in-aid (1877–78); so the Noble School came before Madras University.

nindian-history-124-2.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hunter Commission of 1882:
1. It was associated with W.W. Hunter and dealt with education.
2. It dealt with famine policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nindian-history-124-2.x: The Hunter Commission under W.W. Hunter dealt with education; famine policy was the work of the Strachey Commission.

new.s: The Chalisa famine of 1783–84 mainly affected:
new.x: The Chalisa famine (1783–84), named after Vikram Samvat 1840, hit North India (Delhi, Awadh, Punjab).

new.s: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred under the governorship of:
new.x: The 1770 Bengal famine came under Cartier, when about a third of Bengal's people died; Lytton was the ruler of the 1876–78 Great Famine.

new.s: Which famine is described as the 'Sea of Calamity'?
new.x: The Orissa and Ganjam famine of 1865–66 was called the 'Sea of Calamity' and led to the Campbell Commission.

new.s: About how many people died in the Bengal famine of 1943?
new.x: About 30 lakh (3 million) people died in the 1943 Bengal famine, which led to the Woodhead Commission.

new.s: The Guntur famine of 1832–33 is locally known as:
new.x: The 1832–33 Guntur famine, the most serious South Indian famine, is called Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu.

new.s: Who formed a relief committee during the 1945 famine in Andhra?
new.x: K.S. Gupta formed a relief committee in the 1945 famine.

new.s: How many famines hit Andhra in the late 19th century?
new.x: Andhra suffered 11 famines in the late 19th century.

new.s: The Lyall Famine Commission was appointed under Viceroy:
new.x: The Lyall Commission (1898) followed the 1896–97 famine under Elgin II; MacDonnell (1901) came under Curzon.

new.s: Which was the first famine commission of British India?
new.x: The Campbell Commission (1866), on the Orissa famine, was the first; Woodhead (1944) was the last.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Famine Code, 1883:
1. It was framed on the recommendations of the Strachey Commission.
2. It provided relief works for the able-bodied.
3. It provided gratuitous relief for the old and infirm.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 1883 Code came from the Strachey Commission (1880) and provided relief works for the able-bodied and gratuitous relief for the old and infirm.

new.s: Under the Famine Code of 1883, relief works were meant for the:
new.x: Relief works were for the able-bodied (fit); gratuitous relief was for the old and infirm.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Temple wage:
1. It was fixed by Sir Richard Temple in the 1877 Madras famine.
2. It gave about 1 lb of grain a day on relief works.
3. It was praised as a fair living wage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Temple fixed about 1 lb of grain a day in the 1877 Madras famine; it was criticised as a starvation wage, not praised.

new.s: The idea of public works as famine relief goes back to:
new.x: Kautilya already prescribed seeds, food, tax exemption and public works in famine.

new.s: The construction of the Krishna anicut at Bezwada was supervised by:
new.x: The Krishna anicut (1853–54) was proposed by Col. Henry Atlock Lake and supervised by Charles Orr.

new.s: The main structure of the Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram was completed in:
new.x: Cotton's report came in 1844, sanction in 1846, work began in 1847 and the main structure was finished in April 1852.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (anicut – place) is correctly matched?
new.x: Penna anicut was at Nellore (1860); Godavari was at Dowleswaram, Krishna at Bezwada and the K.C. Canal at Sunkesula.

new.s: In the IPC food-insecurity scale, Phase 4 is:
new.x: The IPC phases are 1 Minimal, 2 Stressed, 3 Crisis, 4 Emergency and 5 Catastrophe/Famine.

new.s: How many phases does the IPC food-insecurity scale have?
new.x: The IPC scale has five phases, from Minimal to Catastrophe/Famine.

new.s: R.C. Dutt's 'Open Letters to Lord Curzon' appeared in:
new.x: R.C. Dutt wrote 'Open Letters to Lord Curzon' in 1900.

new.s: Who led the Anglicists in the education debate?
new.x: Macaulay led the Anglicists with Bentinck and Trevelyan; Colebrooke, Wilson and Duncan were Orientalists.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an Orientalist?
new.x: Charles Trevelyan was an Anglicist; Hastings, Jones and Wilson were Orientalists.

new.s: In the Madras Presidency, Thomas Munro backed:
new.x: Munro supported pathashalas and vernacular schooling, not English-only education.

new.s: Munro's collectorate and tahsildari schools in Madras were closed in:
new.x: After the 1835 resolution, Munro's collectorate and tahsildari schools were closed in 1836.

new.s: Macaulay's Minute on Education is dated:
new.x: Macaulay's Minute is dated 2 February 1835; 19 July 1854 is the date of Wood's Despatch.

new.s: Who is called the 'Father of Modern Western Education in India'?
new.x: Bentinck, who approved Macaulay's Minute, is called the Father of Modern Western Education in India.

new.s: Macaulay wanted English education to create a class of Indians who would act as:
new.x: Macaulay's aim was a class of Indians to act as interpreters between the rulers and the ruled.

new.s: 'A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia' was said by:
new.x: This famous remark comes from Macaulay's Minute of 1835.

new.s: Sir Charles Wood issued his Despatch of 1854 as:
o: President of the Board of Control
new.x: Wood was President of the Board of Control; Dalhousie was the Governor-General, and Macaulay was Law Member and President of the GCPI.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Wood's Despatch, 1854?
new.x: Wood's Despatch rejected downward filtration and asked for mass instruction; it backed grants-in-aid, teacher training and female education.

new.s: The Hartog Committee (1929) was appointed under Viceroy:
new.x: The Hartog Committee came under Irwin; Wavell was Viceroy at the Sargent Plan (1944).

new.s: Which Indian was a member of the Sadler Commission?
new.x: Ashutosh Mukherjee sat on the Sadler Commission; Gurudas Banerjee and Bilgrami were members of the 1902 Raleigh Commission.

new.s: The Raleigh Universities Commission of 1902 led to the Indian Universities Act of:
new.x: The 1902 Commission under Curzon led to the Indian Universities Act 1904, which increased government control.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (body – subject) is correctly matched?
new.x: The Lee Commission (1924) was on civil services; Whitley dealt with labour, Butler with the Indian States and Simon with constitutional reforms.

new.s: Which body of 1927 dealt with the Indian States and the Paramount Power?
new.x: The Butler Committee (1927) dealt with the Indian States and Paramount Power; the Simon Commission was on constitutional reforms.

new.s: Osmania University (1917) was the first Indian university with instruction in:
new.x: Osmania, founded by Mir Osman Ali Khan in 1917, was the first Indian university with a regional language (Urdu) medium.

new.s: Who was the first Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University?
new.x: C.R. Reddy was the first VC of Andhra University (1926); Prakasam set up Sri Venkateswara University.

new.s: The North German missionary society had its Andhra centres at:
new.x: The North German Society worked from Rajahmundry and Eluru (1843); the LMS was at Kadapa, Lutherans at Guntur and American Baptists at Ongole and Nellore.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra University:
1. The Andhra University Act was passed in 1925.
2. It moved to Waltair in 1926.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Act came in 1925; the university opened at Bezawada in 1926 and moved to Waltair only in 1930.

new.s: The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded in:
new.x: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal on 15 January 1784.

new.s: Mayo College at Ajmer (1875) was meant for:
new.x: Mayo College was a school for Indian princes and nobility, which makes it the odd one among early institutions.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813:
1. It set aside Rs 1 lakh a year for education.
2. It admitted missionaries to India.
3. It ended the Company's India trade monopoly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Charter Act 1813 earmarked Rs 1 lakh a year for literature and science, admitted missionaries and ended the India trade monopoly.

new.s: The first Factory Act in India was passed in:
new.x: The first Factory Act (child labour) came in 1881 under Ripon, not 1882.

new.s: The Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883 took place under Viceroy:
new.x: The Famine Code and the Ilbert Bill controversy both belong to 1883, under Ripon.

new.s: The Vernacular Press Act was repealed in 1882 by:
new.x: Lytton passed the Act in 1878 and Ripon repealed it in 1882.

new.s: The Indian Universities Act of 1904 under Curzon aimed at:
new.x: The 1904 Act increased government control of universities; free education 6–14 was the Sargent Plan and the 12-year school was Sadler.

new.s: Which body (1929) examined wastage in primary education?
new.x: The Hartog Committee (1929) reported on wastage in primary education.

new.s: The Sanskrit College at Benaras (1791) was founded by:
new.x: Jonathan Duncan founded the Benaras Sanskrit College; William Jones founded the Asiatic Society (1784).

new.s: Which of the following pairs (institution – founder) is correctly matched?
o: Asiatic Society of Bengal – Richard Wellesley
new.x: Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madrasa (1780); Fort William College was Wellesley's, the Asiatic Society was Jones's and Hindu College was Ram Mohan Roy's and David Hare's.

new.s: The early centres of English education in Andhra were:
new.x: Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry were the early centres of English education in Andhra.

new.s: Madras University was set up in:
new.x: Madras University was one of the three universities of 1857 set up after Wood's Despatch.

new.s: The telegraph link with Europe (1864–69) was made under:
new.x: The telegraph with Europe came in 1864–69 under John Lawrence.

new.s: The first railway line in South India (1856) ran from Royapuram to:
new.x: The first South Indian railway (1 July 1856) ran from Royapuram (Madras) to Wallajah Road (Arcot).

new.s: State railways in India are credited to:
new.x: Railways, post and telegraph are credited to Dalhousie, but state railways to Mayo.

new.s: India's first passenger train of 16 April 1853 covered a distance of:
new.x: The first train ran 34 km from Bori Bunder (Bombay) to Thane.

new.s: Sedition (Section 124A) was added to the IPC in:
new.x: Section 124A made 'exciting disaffection' an offence in 1870, under Mayo.

new.s: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act 1908 and the Indian Press Act 1910 were passed under:
new.x: Both Acts came in the Minto II era, though they are not cause and effect.

new.s: Who is called the 'liberator of the Indian press'?
new.x: Metcalfe's Act of 1835 repealed the 1823 Licensing Regulations, earning him the title 'liberator of the Indian press'.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vernacular Press Act, 1878?
o: It applied to English papers as well
It allowed no appeal to a court
new.x: The Act applied only to Indian-language papers, not English ones; that is why it was called discriminatory.

new.s: In the World Press Freedom Index 2026, India ranked:
new.x: India ranked 157th of 180 in the World Press Freedom Index 2026.

new.s: The RNI is now known as the:
new.x: Under the 2023 Act the RNI became the Press Registrar General of India.

new.s: Sambad Kaumudi (1821) of Ram Mohan Roy was published in:
new.x: Sambad Kaumudi was Bengali; Mirat-ul-Akhbar was Persian and Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq Urdu.

new.s: Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq (1870) was started by:
new.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan started the Urdu journal Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq in 1870.

new.s: Kesari (1881) was founded by:
new.x: Tilak founded the Marathi paper Kesari in 1881.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about The Bengalee:
1. It was founded by Girish Chandra Ghosh in 1862.
2. Surendranath Banerjea ran it from 1879.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Bengalee was founded by Girish Chandra Ghosh in 1862 and run by Surendranath Banerjea from 1879.

new.s: Krishna Patrika (1902, Machilipatnam) was founded by:
new.x: Konda Venkatappayya, with Dasu Narayana Rao, founded Krishna Patrika; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (paper – founder) is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Andhra Kesari was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's paper, not Veeresalingam's.

new.s: Andhra Patrika started in 1908 as a weekly from:
new.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao started Andhra Patrika as a weekly in Bombay; it later became a daily from Madras.
